expectedText:
TIME OFF TO VOTE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Corp.

ABOUT THIS TIME OFF TO VOTE INFORMATION SHEET
This Time Off to Vote — Information Sheet describes the paid-time-off-to-vote rights created by California Elections Code §§ 14000–14002, part of the "Privileges of Voters" chapter of the Elections Code, as it relates to the working relationship between Jordan Lee and Acme Corp. It summarizes selected requirements of that law: the condition under which a voter is entitled to take paid time off work to vote, the two-hour cap and default timing on that paid time, the advance notice an employee must give the employer, and the employer's own duty to post notice of these rights before each statewide election.

Elections Code §§ 14000 through 14002 are not the whole of the "Privileges of Voters" chapter. Section 14003, in the same chapter, addresses a voter's exemption from militia duty on election day — an unrelated subject this document does not cover. Section 14004, added to the same chapter effective January 1, 2020, separately bars an employer from requiring or requesting that an employee bring a vote-by-mail ballot to work or vote it at work; that is a distinct right from the paid-time-off right described here, and this document does not address it.

This information sheet is not itself the notice Elections Code § 14001 requires an employer to post, does not itself determine whether Jordan Lee has sufficient time to vote outside working hours on any particular election day, and does not determine that any particular policy of Acme Corp.'s is or is not compliant with California law.

ENTITLEMENT TO PAID TIME OFF TO VOTE
Under California law, if a voter does not have sufficient time outside of working hours to vote at a statewide election, the voter may, without loss of pay, take off enough working time that, when added to the voting time available outside working hours, will enable the voter to vote.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "If a voter does not have sufficient time outside of working hours to vote at a statewide election, the voter may, without loss of pay, take off enough working time that, when added to the voting time available outside of working hours, will enable the voter to vote."
  — Cal. Elec. Code § 14000(a) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov official text), California Elections Code, time off to vote — entitlement condition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=ELEC&sectionNum=14000)
  Known gap: This is subdivision (a) of Elections Code § 14000. The amount-and-timing clause and the advance-notice clause in this set cite subdivisions (b) and (c) of this SAME section § 14000, not independent statutes; the posting clause cites the genuinely separate § 14001, and the applicability clause cites the genuinely separate § 14002. This clause states only the entitlement condition itself — it does not state the amount of paid time allowed, when it must be taken, or the notice an employee must give, all of which are covered in the other clauses of this set. The statute does not define "sufficient time" or "statewide election"; whether a given employee's schedule leaves sufficient time to vote, and whether a given election is a "statewide election," are questions of fact this clause does not resolve.

AMOUNT OF PAID VOTING TIME AND WHEN IT IS TAKEN
No more than two hours of the time taken off to vote is without loss of pay. That paid time off is taken only at the beginning or end of the regular working shift — whichever allows the most free time for voting and the least time off from the shift — unless the employee and employer otherwise mutually agree.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "No more than two hours of the time taken off for voting shall be without loss of pay. The time off for voting shall be only at the beginning or end of the regular working shift, whichever allows the most free time for voting and the least time off from the regular working shift, unless otherwise mutually agreed."
  — Cal. Elec. Code § 14000(b) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov official text), California Elections Code, time off to vote — two-hour paid cap and default timing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=ELEC&sectionNum=14000)
  Known gap: This is subdivision (b) of the same Elections Code § 14000 addressed in the entitlement clause and the advance-notice clause in this set, not an independent section. The default timing (start or end of shift) applies only "unless otherwise mutually agreed"; this clause does not state what governs if the employee and employer do not reach such an agreement, and does not say whether time beyond two hours may be taken unpaid. It does not restate the entitlement condition in subdivision (a) or the notice duty in subdivision (c), both addressed in separate clauses.

ADVANCE NOTICE REQUIRED FROM THE EMPLOYEE
If, on the third working day before election day, the employee knows or has reason to believe that time off will be necessary to be able to vote, the employee must give the employer at least two working days' notice that time off for voting is desired.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "If the employee on the third working day prior to the day of election, knows or has reason to believe that time off will be necessary to be able to vote on election day, the employee shall give the employer at least two working days’ notice that time off for voting is desired, in accordance with this section."
  — Cal. Elec. Code § 14000(c) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov official text), California Elections Code, time off to vote — employee's advance-notice duty (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=ELEC&sectionNum=14000)
  Known gap: This is subdivision (c) of the same Elections Code § 14000 addressed in the entitlement clause and the amount-and-timing clause in this set, not an independent section. The statute frames the trigger for this duty as the employee's knowledge or reason to believe — as of the third working day before the election — that time off will be necessary, rather than a simple flat two-day-before deadline; this clause does not restate that distinction beyond quoting the statutory language. It does not specify a required form (written or otherwise) for the notice, which the statute does not itself prescribe, and does not state the amount of paid time available (subdivision (b)) or the entitlement condition (subdivision (a)), both addressed in separate clauses.

EMPLOYER'S WORKPLACE POSTING DUTY
Not less than 10 days before every statewide election, every employer must keep posted conspicuously at the place of work — or, if that is not practicable, elsewhere where it can be seen as employees come or go to their place of work — a notice setting forth the time-off-to-vote provisions described above.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Not less than 10 days before every statewide election, every employer shall keep posted conspicuously at the place of work, if practicable, or elsewhere where it can be seen as employees come or go to their place of work, a notice setting forth the provisions of Section 14000."
  — Cal. Elec. Code § 14001 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov official text), California Elections Code, time off to vote — employer's workplace-posting duty (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=ELEC&sectionNum=14001)
  Known gap: Elections Code § 14001 is an independent section from § 14000, addressed in the entitlement, amount-and-timing, and advance-notice clauses above; this posting clause does not restate those other clauses' content beyond referencing it collectively. The statute requires the notice to be posted "not less than 10 days before every statewide election" and to "set forth the provisions of Section 14000," but does not prescribe the notice's specific wording, format, or size — a separate drafting clause in this set (the sample workplace notice) offers text intended to satisfy that content requirement, not an official state-issued poster. This clause does not address § 14002's extension of the posting duty to public employers, or § 14004's separate vote-by-mail-ballot provision, both left out of the authority clauses in this set (see the applicability clause below and the purpose clause's discussion of § 14004).

APPLIES TO BOTH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EMPLOYERS
The paid-time-off-to-vote entitlement, the advance-notice duty, and the employer's workplace-posting duty apply to all public agencies and their employees, as well as to employers and employees in private industry.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Sections 14000, 14001, and 14004 shall apply to all public agencies and the employees thereof, as well as to employers and employees in private industry."
  — Cal. Elec. Code § 14002 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov official text, as amended by Stats. 2019, Ch. 223 (AB 17), eff. Jan. 1, 2020), California Elections Code, time off to vote — applies to public and private employers alike (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=ELEC&sectionNum=14002)
  Known gap: Elections Code § 14002 is an independent section from § 14000 and § 14001, addressed in no other clause in this set. As amended effective January 1, 2020 (Stats. 2019, Ch. 223 (AB 17)), it extends §§ 14000, 14001, AND 14004 to public agencies and their employees as well as private employers; that same 2019 act added § 14004 to the chapter. This clause does not draft any public-agency-specific variation of these duties, and does not cover § 14004's separate substantive right — which bars an employer from requiring or requesting that an employee bring a vote-by-mail ballot to work or vote it at work — a related but genuinely distinct provision from the time-off-to-vote right covered by this clause set, omitted here rather than folded into this citation.

SAMPLE WORKPLACE NOTICE — TIME OFF TO VOTE
The following sample notice is offered to help Acme Corp. satisfy the content Elections Code § 14001 requires — a posted notice "setting forth the provisions of Section 14000" — and is not itself an official state-issued poster:

NOTICE TO EMPLOYEES — TIME OFF TO VOTE

If you do not have sufficient time outside of your working hours to vote at a statewide election, you may, without loss of pay, take off enough working time that, when added to the voting time available outside of working hours, will enable you to vote.

No more than two hours of the time taken off for voting will be without loss of pay. The time off for voting will be only at the beginning or end of your regular working shift, whichever allows the most free time for voting and the least time off from your regular working shift, unless you and Acme Corp. otherwise mutually agree.

If you know or have reason to believe, on the third working day before the election, that you will need time off to vote, you must give Acme Corp. at least two working days' notice that you desire time off for voting.

Acme Corp. will keep this notice posted conspicuously at the place of work, or elsewhere where it can be seen as employees come or go from work, not less than 10 days before every statewide election.

—
